3. Krishnapada Biswas and others, the predecessors of the respondents herein as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.1208 of 1983 against Saburannessa Bibi and others, the predecessors of the appellants, seeking declaration of title in the suit land, which consisted of 30 decimals of land situated in plot No.307 and also 03 decimals of land situated in other plot, both under khatian No.133 of Mouza and P.S. Jhenaidah and also for recovery of khas possession thereof on the averments that above plot No.307 measuring 63 decimals of land belonged to Fazar Ali and others. Subsequently, Sattendra Nath became the owner of the same, and then on 15th Chaitra B.S, 1354, Sattendra Nath leased 30 decimals of land situated on the northern side of plot No.307 to Haripada, his servant, who then constructing a house started living therein. But the survey record was wrongly prepared in the name of Sattendra Nath. On 15th Kartick,1375 B.S, Jagadish disclosed to Haripada that the record of right in respect of the suit land stands in the name of Sattendra and he had purchased the suit land from Sattendra Nath along with other lands. After coming to know about the same, Haripada filed Miscellaneous Case No.566 of 1969 under section 143(a) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for correction of the record of right and then the above miscellaneous case was stayed with a direction to the other side to file a regular title suit by 20.05.1970 and such suit not being filed, decision was given in favour of Haripada on 15.06.1970. During the liberation war, Haripada was shot dead in his own house. From suit plot No.307, which contained 60 decimals of land(but wrongly written 63 decimals in khatian), Jagadish purchased only 33 decimals of land from Sattendra Nath but he in his kabala from Sattendra Nath, fraudulently included the entire land of the plot, which was owned by Haripada and Amanat Mollah. Haripada died leaving his wife Bimala Bala, who sold 03 decimals of land to Manju Rani, respondent No.6 of Civil Revision No.286 of 2001. Then Bimala Bala on 24.7.73 sold 10 decimals and on 01.09.1975 sold 17 decimals of land to plaintiff No.1 and Basanti Bala. They dug a pond in 15 decimals of purchased land. Basanti Bala on 14.7.1976 sold 02 decimals of land to Monto Kumar. The defendant earlier filed Title Suit No.869 of 1981, which ended on filing a solenama which was forcefully obtained by the defendants from the plaintiff. Thereafter, defendants forcibly took possession of the suit land on 15.11.1981. Then on 10.10.1982 defendant constructed a straw-hut on the bank of the pond which is situated within the suit land. 

 13. The appellate Court, on the other hand, came to the finding that the plaintiff claimed that Haripada took settlement of 30+3=33 decimals of land from Sattendra Nath and that on perusal of the record it appeared that no document could be produced to substantiate the claim of settle-ment. The appellate Court also came to the finding that admittedly Haripada was a servant of Sattendra Nath and that it was not believable that Sattendra Nath after settling the suit land to his servant would get the R.S. khatian recorded in his own name in respect of the said land. The appellate Court held that it was believable that subsequently by two deeds of sale, Jagadish and Amanat Molla purchased the entire land of suit plot No.307 measuring 63 decimals of land. 

 17. The plaintiff claimed that Sattendra Nath settled .33 acre of land to Haripada on 15th Chaitra, 1354 B.S. The plaintiff, however, could not produce any registered deed or dakhila and not even oral evidence to substantiate his claim. P.W.1 in his evidence stated that he did not have any personal knowledge about the alleged settlement. P.W.2 Lutfor Rahman in his evidence stated that when Sattendra Nath settled the suit land to Haripada, his father wrote the dakhila and that his father was the 'Gomasta' of Sattendra Nath and that on the date of his deposition, he was aged at 56/57 years. The appellate Court computed the age of P.W.2 Lutfor Rahman and found that at the time of alleged settlement his age was about 9/10 years. Therefore, the appellate Court discarded his evidence as being a child witness. The plaintiff claimed that Haripada took settlement of .30 acre of land from the suit plot and .03 acre of land from other plot but it appears that the khatian was prepared in the name of Sattendra Nath. It is also admitted that Haripada was admittedly the servant of Sattendra Nath. Therefore, it creates doubt that Sattendra Nath after giving the settlement of the suit land to his servant Haripada would get the suit land recorded in his own name. On the contrary, it appears to be believable that subsequently Sattendra on the basis of two registered kabalas sold the entire land of the disputed plot to Jagadish and Amanath Molla. 

 18. The learned Assistant Judge relied upon exhibit-D, the certified copy of the Miscellaneous Case No.566 of 1969. But before institution of the aforesaid miscellaneous case, Sattendra Nath sold the entire land of the suit plot to Jagadish and Amanth Molla. Therefore, after relinquishment of the right of Sattendra Nath in respect of the suit land, Haripada filed the miscellaneous case for correction of khatian against Sattendra Nath. The appellate Court, therefore, held that this miscellaneous case was collusive and fraudulent and as such, the decision of the miscellaneous case for correction of khatian was ineffective. It was revealed that the defendants were not parties to the said miscellaneous case and that the defendant disputed the very existence and effectiveness of the said miscellaneous case for correction of khatian. The appellate Court also came to the finding that possession of this defendant is admitted in .15 acre of land out of the suit land measuring .30 acre of land. On the other hand, the plaintiff claimed that he was dispossessed from 05/06 acre of land. Record reveals that the plaintiff purchased the suit land in 1973 and 1975 and prior to that the defendant acquired title thereto. The appellate Court also noted that D.W.2, a child witness, tried to prove the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land but that his evidence was dis-carded by the appellate Court on the ground that at the relevant time he was child witness aged about 9/10 years.
